title: SMI Ergodic Indicator
summary: A double smoothed momentum line with a signal line and their difference as a histogram, for reading trend and momentum turns.
description:
The SMI Ergodic Indicator is a double smoothed momentum oscillator built on William Blau's true strength index. On each bar the change in the source from the previous bar is taken, and both that change and its absolute size are smoothed twice: first by an exponential average over `Long Length` bars (20 by default), then by one over `Short Length` bars (5 by default). The **SMI** line is 100 times the smoothed change divided by the smoothed size, so it runs from -100 to 100.

A **Signal** line, an exponential average of the SMI over `Signal Length` bars, follows it, and the **Oscillator** histogram shows the SMI minus the signal: green at or above zero, red below.
howToRead:
The SMI above zero means the smoothed changes have been mostly upward, below zero mostly downward, and the distance from zero shows how one-sided they were. A cross of the SMI above its signal line, where the histogram turns from red to green, is read as momentum turning up; a cross below as momentum turning down. Crossings far from zero, after a long run in one direction, carry more weight than those near it.

The double smoothing removes most bar to bar noise but adds lag, and in a sideways market the two lines weave around each other, so the histogram flips often without a lasting move.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The price series whose changes are measured. Close is the default.

settings.label: Long Length
settings.description: Bars in the first, longer exponential average of the changes. A larger value gives a smoother, slower line. 20 is the usual value.

settings.label: Short Length
settings.description: Bars in the second, shorter exponential average applied after the first. 5 is the usual value.

settings.label: Signal Length
settings.description: Bars in the exponential average of the SMI that forms the signal line and sets the histogram. 5 is the usual value.

faq.q: How is it related to the true strength index?
faq.a: The SMI line is the true strength index of the source with a long length of 20 and a short length of 5. The study adds a signal line and the histogram of their difference.
The gap between the SMI and its signal line. It turns green when the SMI rises above the signal and red when it falls below, so its colour changes mark the crossings.

faq.q: Why can it not go beyond 100 or -100?
faq.a: The smoothed change can never be larger in size than the smoothed size of the changes, so their ratio stays between -1 and 1 before it is scaled by 100.
